rows.headline: Apparel exports surge 20% in October driven by currency depreciation
rows.hook: Currency gains drive value over volume

modes.bear: Subdued volume growth signals weak consumer demand in global markets, making export growth overly reliant on currency tailwinds.
modes.bull: Currency depreciation boosts rupee realization on export orders, expanding margins for textile manufacturers despite flat volume.
modes.simple: Indian clothing exports earned 20% more money in October mostly because the rupee fell against the dollar, even though actual clothing shipments did not increase much.

rows.summary: India's apparel exports grew 20% year-on-year in October, largely aided by rupee depreciation against the dollar. However, underlying volume growth remains subdued due to persistent demand softness in key Western markets. Textile players are seeing higher realization per shipment despite sluggish order quantities. Indian retail investors with exposure to export-oriented garment manufacturers should monitor order volume trends rather than just headline value growth.
rows.why_it_matters: Higher earnings for garment exporters despite weak underlying shipment volumes.
rows.winners_losers: Textile exporters gain / volume-dependent players hurt
